title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Oil jumped (Brent >$106, WTI ~$93, +1.5%) after a Houthi missile hit Riyadh's airport and Russian strikes hit Ukrainian energy sites despite Trump's declared "ceasefire"; US stocks closed mixed Monday — Dow +0.4%, S&P 500 -0.06%, Nasdaq -0.4% — with memory-chip weakness also pressuring tech. 10-year Treasury yield holding near 24-year highs (~5.24%).

Companies: Q3 bank earnings season kicks off today before the bell — JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Wells Fargo and Citigroup report, with UnitedHealth, J&J and Domino's also on deck; FactSet projects 29.5% S&P 500 Q3 earnings growth.

Companies: Starbucks confirmed it won't bid for Chipotle (shares +1.7%) while Chipotle fell 3.8% as takeover speculation fizzled; SWI Group, operator of ex-FTX bitcoin-mining assets, raised ~$900M to pivot into AI data centers, shares +16%.
Macro/Policy: FHFA now lets mortgage lenders use VantageScore alongside FICO for Fannie/Freddie loans — likely more approvals, but possibly higher default risk.
Macro/Policy: Today's data (NFIB optimism, existing home sales, ADP employment) sets up for Wednesday's September CPI and Thursday's PPI, the last big inflation prints before the Oct 28 FOMC meeting.
Macro/Policy: Strategists flag the Iran conflict, stretched 2027 EPS estimates, midterm elections and the Fed's rate path as key risks heading into earnings season.
